subject: Startups
title: The Worst VC Misses
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Worst VC Misses.

hook.text: Excite could have bought Google for $750K in 1999. They said no. Google is now worth over $2 trillion.

buildup.text: Bessemer Venture Partners passed on Apple, eBay, Google, Facebook, and PayPal. They call it their 'anti-portfolio.'

discovery.text: Most VC misses happen because the idea seems too small, too weird, or too early at the time of the pitch.

twist.text: Bessemer published their anti-portfolio publicly. Owning their misses became a brilliant marketing move.

climax.text: Even the best VCs miss giants. The lesson: conviction matters more than consensus when it comes to big bets.

punchline.text: Every great VC has a graveyard of deals they passed on.

quiz.question: What is Bessemer Venture Partners' 'anti-portfolio'?
options: A list of companies they regrettably passed on
